plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked metallurgical cross-section shows 200-atmosphere H₂ at 500°C diffusing into carbon steel to form explosive methane (CH₄) blisters, alongside Carl Bosch's double-walled solution: a thin carbon-free soft-iron inner liner inside a thick carbon-steel outer shell drilled with 'Bosch holes' that vent diffusing H₂ harmlessly.

teach_overlay.label: 200 ATM H₂ → SOFT-IRON LINER + PERFORATED STEEL 'BOSCH HOLES'
teach_overlay.detail: Inked cross-section diagram on period paper of Carl Bosch's double-walled reactor: 200 atm / 500°C N₂ + H₂ core → thin carbon-free soft-iron inner liner → perforated strong carbon-steel outer shell drilled with 'Bosch holes' venting diffusing H₂ safely
teach_overlay.scale: hydrogen atoms are so small they slip straight between the iron atoms of solid red-hot cannon steel and rot it from within — until Bosch drilled tiny escape holes in the outer armour
